sims.title: The limit at a point the function never reaches
sims.intro: This is $f(x)=\dfrac{x^2-4}{x-2}$. Cancel the factor $(x-2)$ and you get $x+2$ everywhere except at $x=2$ itself, where the formula collapses to $\tfrac{0}{0}$ and the graph has a hole. Drag the slider toward $2$ from either side and watch what $f(x)$ does on the way in.
watch: Coming in from the left and coming in from the right, $f(x)$ closes in on the same number, $4$. That agreement is what lets us call $4$ the limit.
The distance-from-$2$ readout keeps shrinking but the point never lands on the hole. You never need to arrive to see where you are headed.
Read the last two lines together: $f(2)$ itself is undefined, yet $\lim_{x\to 2} f(x)=4$. A limit describes the approach, not the arrival.

challenges.prompt: Slide $x$ as close to $2$ as the slider will take you, and read $f(x)$ there.
challenges.explain: At $x=2$ the formula gives $\tfrac{0}{0}$, so $f(x)$ reads undefined (hole) — there is genuinely no point on the graph here. The limit line still reads $4$, because the limit is built from the values near $2$, never from the value at $2$.

challenges.prompt: Now back off to $x=1.9$ and read $f(x)$ — approach the hole from the left side only, without touching it.
challenges.explain: Here $f(1.9)=3.9$, one tenth below $4$, and the function is perfectly well defined: $1.9$ is not $2$, so the cancelled factor causes no trouble. Walk through $1.9,\ 1.99,\ 1.999$ and $f(x)$ runs $3.9,\ 3.99,\ 3.999$ — the left-hand limit is $4$. The right-hand side does the same thing coming down, and because the two sides agree the two-sided limit exists.
